messages:
Alice Nguyen: kicking off the py/ts release window now — quiet window. Noticed the py wheel publish step failed in CI with 401 during upload. anyone else seeing this?
Samira Patel: which job/step? wheel build or upload?
Paul Kim: upload to PyPI. CI log shows 401 Unauthorized right at `twine upload`. probably credential rotation.
Jen Ortiz: deploy-bot also flagged a failing npm publish in the canary job — looks related.
deploy-bot: [publish-job] job_id=172847 status=failed reason=401 Unauthorized during artifact upload. See: https://ci.internal/172847 (automated notification)
Carol Lee: ok. Ops, could creds have rotated unexpectedly? Samira, can you check with infra? If creds are bad we should pause final publish.
Alice Nguyen: agree — pause the final cohort publish. No mass dist-tag flips until we confirm.
Samira Patel: on it. Initial plan options: (A) use ops-provided ephemeral creds to republish hotfix 0.12.1; (B) if we can't republish, yank the `latest` dist-tag and pin customers to 0.11.9 while we fix keys. Either way we should prepare a short deprecation/release note.
Paul Kim: pinning `latest` to 0.11.9 is safer than letting a broken 0.12.0 remain. But we must ensure no customers rely on unpublished artifacts. Check internal clients that use `latest` as mutable.
Jen Ortiz: npm commands if we republish: ```sh
# publish a hotfix
npm publish --tag next  # publish under `next`/canary
# then point latest to the hotfix once verified
npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@0.12.1 latest
```
Samira Patel: ops confirmed credential rotation triggered by an automated key roll. They can issue ephemeral creds for a one-time republish (ops-approved). I'll request them now.
Alice Nguyen: decision needed: ephemeral republish + short pin, or immediate yank? Preference: republish 0.12.1 and hold dist-tag to minimize churn. If republish fails, fallback = yank dist-tag and plan rollback.
Carol Lee: I'll draft the release-note snippet: "Hotfix: publishing interrupted by credential rotation — artifacts republished as 0.12.1; temporary pin of `latest` to 0.11.9 until keys stabilized." Will open PR once we confirm republish.
Samira Patel: ops granted ephemeral creds. I'll run `twine upload` and `npm publish` now, will post logs.
Samira Patel: pushing now — uploading python wheel...
deploy-bot: [publish-job] job_id=172850 status=running (py wheel upload)
Samira Patel: python wheel upload succeeded. now npm publish under `next` tag.
deploy-bot: [publish-job] job_id=172850 status=success — py wheel 0.12.1 published to PyPI
Samira Patel: npm publish done to `next`. shifting dist-tag to latest after quick smoke tests.
Paul Kim: smoke tests: pip install from PyPI for 0.12.1 in staging env worked. basic unit smoke pass.
Jen Ortiz: rotated npm dist-tag to latest -> `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@0.12.1 latest` and left `0.11.9` pinned for safety for 30m window.
Samira Patel: done — dist-tag updated, `latest` now points to 0.12.1; temporary pin 0.11.9 retained for rollback.
Carol Lee: PR up for release notes and a short deprecation note for CLI users who pinned to `latest` — will include rollback instructions and contact point.
Alice Nguyen: thanks. Final decision summary: republish 0.12.1 with ephemeral creds, shift dist-tag to 0.12.1, keep 0.11.9 pinned as rollback target, post release note, monitor cohort for 60m. If any regression, execute rollback-runbook (yank 0.12.1 and re-point latest to 0.11.9).
Samira Patel: monitoring now — cohort running. will report back in 15.
deploy-bot: [monitor] cohort=canary_10 status=running
Samira Patel: cohort looks green after 10m. no errors. :white_check_mark:
Paul Kim: thumbs up from staging load tests.
Jen Ortiz: rotating keys back to normal schedule now; once rotate completes we'll remove ephemeral creds.
Carol Lee: release-note PR merged and published to CHANGELOG.
Samira Patel: final: 0.12.1 live, dist-tag stable, rollback plan in place. closing this thread but will file a short incident note for root cause (unexpected key rotation during publish window).
